answer: For every n in the stated domain, put N=binom(n,2), D=lcm(1,2,…,n^(n−2)), b=N+1, and δ(z)=floor(1/(1+z²)). For each integer 0≤m<2^N, let A_m be the symmetric zero-diagonal matrix whose entries above the diagonal, in lexicographic order, are the N binary digits of m, starting with the least significant digit. Set d_i=Σ_j(A_m)_{ij} and L_m=diag(d_1,…,d_n)−A_m. Define K_m=det L_m[{1,…,n}\{2}], F_m=det L_m[{3,…,n}], w_m=(1−δ(K_m))∏_{i=2}^n δ(d_i−d_1), and e_m=Dnd_1F_m/(K_m+δ(K_m)), where brackets denote principal submatrices. With S_n=Σ_{m=0}^{2^N−1} w_m 2^(b e_m), the exact formula is t_n=(1/D) floor(log_2(S_n)/(binom(n,2)+1)).
